subject: NOTE:6b819414-95a3-46fc-b77d-17292d1403c7
evidence:
Procedure
Total left hip replacement

History of Presenting Complaint
Site: L hip Onset: Gradual overthe past 4 yrs, progressively worsening Character: Deep, aching pain Radiates: Occasionally radiates to the L thigh Associations: Stiffness, reduced ROM, difficulty walking Timing: Constant pain, worse at night and after prolonged activity Exacerbating factors: Weight-bearing activities, prolonged standing or walking Severity: 8/10 at worst, 4/10 at best with analgesics

Past Medical History
- HTN
- Hyperlipidemia
- Mild osteopenia

Medications
- Paracetamol 500mg twice daily
- Ibuprofen 400mg as needed

Allergies
No known drug allergies

Social History
- Lives in a bungalow with her partner
- Independent in activities of daily living (ADLs) but uses a walking stick for mobility
- Non-smoker
- Drinks 6-8 units of alcohol per week
- No recreational drug use
- Retired school teacher
- Engages in light stretchnig exercises but has significantly reduced activity levels due to hip pain

Family History
- Mother had HTN and osteoarthritis
- Father had type 2 diabetes and HLD

On Examination
- Patient appeared comfortable at rest but had a slightly antalgic gait due to left hip pain
- CVS: Normal heart sounds, no murmurs, no peripheral oedema
- Resp: Clear breath sounds bilaterally, no wheeze or crackles
- Abdo: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly, normal bowel sounds
- MSK: Left hip joint tender to palpation, reduced ROM (especially internaland external rotation), mild muscle wasting noted in the left thigh.

subject: NOTE:6b819414-95a3-46fc-b77d-17292d1403c7
evidence:

- Bloods: Mild anaemia (Hb 10.8 g/dL), other results including renal and LFTs within normal limits
- Pending: None

Plan
- Prescribed Ferous Sulfate 200 mg once daily to address mild anaemia
- Requested GP review of antihypertensive medications to optimise BP control pre-operatively
- Advised patient to continue current analgesics as needed
- Reinforced importance of maintaining mobility and encouraged gentle exercises within pain limits
- Confirmed no allergies and ensured patient understood the procedure, associated risks, and the importance of optimising her health before surgery
- Scheduled for surgery as planned on 02/01/26

- Significant cartilage erosion
- Osteophyte formation consistent with end-stage OA

- Severely eroded cartilage
- Osteophytes from the R knee joint

Minimal

None

- Antibiotic prophylaxis with cefuroxime 1.5g IV for 24h post-op

- Monitor for signs of infection or thrombosis
- Encourage mobilisation with physiotherapy as per post-op protocol
- Continue routine post-op care and pain management as required

GA with additional spinal anaesthesia for optimal pain management

Posterolateral approach to the left hip

End-stage OA of the left hip

- Subchondral bone sclerosis consistent with advanced OA
- Surrounding soft tissue appeared healthy with no signs of inflammation or infection

- Damaged articular cartilage
- Underlying subchondral bone from the left femoral head adn acetabulum

Prostheses or Implants
- Cementless acetabular c omponent
- Cementless femoral stem with modular head

Closure Technique
- Deep layers closed with absorbable sutures
- Skin closed with absorbable subcuticular sutures
- Sterile ddressing applied over the incision

Estimated Blood Loss
300 mL

Complications
None encountered

Post-Operative Care
- Prescribe Cefuroxime 1.5 g IV every 8 hours for 24 hours for infection prophylaxis
- Start enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily for thromboprophylaxs
- Regular p aracetamol 1 g every 6 hours and ibuprofen 400 mg every 8 hours for post-op pain management
- Prescribe morphine 10 mg PRN for breakthrough pain
- Schedule initial physio session the following morning

Plan
- Encourage mobilisation as per physio guidance starting on 04/01/26

subject: NOTE:eb372a15-b211-4178-a0b5-9ed25fde95d4
evidence:
Ethel Joanne Duffy

Anaesthesia Type
GA

Procedure
Total left hip replacement

Incision
Posterolateral approach to the left hip

Diagnosis
End-stag OA of the left hip

Findings
- Severe cartilage degeneration noted in the acetabulum and femoral head
- Surrounding soft tissues appeared unremarkable with no evidece of acute inflammation or infection

Tissue Removed
- Degenerated femoral head of the left hip
- Damaged cartilage from the acetabular surface

Prostheses or Implants
- Cemented acetabular cup
- Cemented femoral stem with amodular head

Closure Technique
- Layers closed using absorbable wsutures for deep tissue
- Skin closed with staples
- Sterile dressing applied

Estimated Blood Loss
250 mL

Complications
None

Post-Operative Care
- Prophylactic enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily for 4 weeks to reduce risk of DVT
- Oral oxycodone 5 mg every 4â€“6 hours as needed for pain control
- No further doses of IV cefuroxime required after intraoperative admiinistration

Plan
- Encourage mobilisation with physio startnig on postoperative day 1
- Monitor for signs of infection or thromboembolic events
- Reassess pain management requirements daily
- Send removed tissue (degenerative femoral head and damaged cartilage) for histopathology

Additional Notes
- Consultant oversight provided by Dr.
